• 1336 IC: Inspired by a dream, Kaom leads five hundred warriors north and into the Highgate 
mines where Malachai and the Beast reside, but goes mad and slaughters his own men
• When Kaom and his men don't return, his niece Hyrri takes the role of queen and leads the 
remaining Karui in Wraeclast back to Ngamakanui
• Queen Hyrri later leads an army "to deal with a strange threat on the edge of Ngamakanui," but 
they become trapped in the Domain of Timeless Conflict and never return
• Queen Ahuana, Hyrri's daughter, dissolves the monarchy and establishes a council of chieftains to 
rule the still-united Karui tribes; some form of this council remains in present day
• ca. 1356 IC: Deshret goes to Highgate, seals the entrance, and charges her akhara with guarding it
• Deshret is killed by Voll, who has been twisted into a monster and still remains outside Highgate 
with his men; he keeps her banner; her soul becomes trapped in the mines
THE RISE AND FALL OF ORIATH
• 1336 IC: The Cataclysm doesn't affect the island of Oriath, which becomes a theocracy ruled by the 
Templars after the fall of the Eternal Empire
• Lycia makes a pact with the Scourge demon Beidat for immortality and begins luring adventurers 
into the Sanctum for entertainment (may have happened earlier)
• ca. 1450 IC: Daresso gives Merveil the Star of Wraeclast and they marry; she turns into a sea 
monster and flees to Wraeclast, where she lures sailors to their deaths to feed her horde of children
• Daresso leaves in search of a cure, but winds up as a thrall of Malachai's Nightmare like Kaom
• Weylam Roth tries to revive his fading reputation by slaying Merveil, but is eaten alive by her
• ca. 1568 IC: Sigmund Fairgraves disappears after setting sail for Wraeclast
• High Templar Venarius orders Valdo Caeserius to repair a mysterious device found in Wraeclast; 
the device opens a portal to the dreamlands
• 1579 IC: Venarius frees The Elder and it feeds on his memories; Valdo traps himself in the 
dreamlands with The Elder to fight it, becoming the Shaper
• 1579 IC: Dominus replaces Venarius as high templar; he begins exiling undesirables to Wraeclast, 
where they are captured and experimented on by Piety

- 464 -
• An unknown group of researchers works to duplicate unique items; their research results in a 
catastrophe that cracks the sky and their outposts are abandoned (may have happened earlier)
• A rebellion occurs in Kalguur but fails; a group of Kalguurans flee to Wraeclast, ostensibly seeking 
answers to what happened during their earlier colonisation; their outpost grows into Kingsmarch
• ca. 1599 IC: Catarina orchestrates the destruction of the Order of the Djinn and creates the 
Immortal Syndicate to establish a new government in Wraeclast, but is later killed
• 1599 IC: The POE player is exiled and the events of POE begin
• 1599 IC: Venarius gets free of The Elder and wanders Wraeclast as an amnesiac spirit, calling 
himself Cavas; he discovers a place called the Memory Nexus
• Venarius regains his memory and finds he now has the power to change people's memories; he 
attempts to use this to manipulate them to unite under his rule and fight a demonic threat
• 1599 IC: A woman known as The Last to Die (probably an alternate Alva) appears in Wraeclast, 
saying there are many alternate Wraeclasts and all are being taken over by the demonic Scourge; so 
far only one Wraeclast has survived, but it is ruled by Venarius and "you don't want to go there"
• 1600 IC: Kitava is defeated; rebuilding Oriath begins; the POE player sails off for a holiday
AFTER THE FALL OF ORIATH
• 1600 IC: Innocence goes into exile in the south; Sin goes into hiding with the Seed of Corruption
• 1600 IC: Zana Caeserius recruits former exiles to search the Atlas for her father Valdo; they defeat 
The Elder but one of them, Sirus, is lost; other eldritch entities begin to appear in the Atlas
• Sirus reappears, now insane, and Oriath is destroyed a second time; most of the residents flee and 
are taken in by the Karui on an island south of Wraeclast
• 1601 IC: The POE player arrives at the island; POE endgame (investigating the Atlas) begins
• The Twilight Order, having remained behind in Oriath, emerges from secrecy and rebuilds
• Oriana discovers the existence of the Seed of Corruption and devises a plan; she travels to the 
Vastiri and forms an alliance with the Faridun
• Oriana travels to Ogham, marries Count Geonor, and begins to manipulate him
• 1619 IC: The Seed of Corruption is stolen from Sin by Geonor's forces; the events of POE II begin

- 465 -
APPENDIX B: CHARACTERS
PRECURSORS
Currently no named Precursors are known.
PRIMEVALS
Uzaza, the First King: a man who helped his people find a place to settle after a life-long journey, 
and helped them get fish out of a frozen river to live on.
Putembo: a king and tyrant who used slaves to quarry stone for his fortress.
Aul, a.k.a. Ahn, the Last King: a slave who was made to quarry stone for Putembo's fortress. He 
eventually overthrew Putembo and became king himself, and was crowned Ahn. He was 
renowned for his leadership, as well as being fearless, ferocious and a tactical genius. However, 
he was also known for being a tyrant. During the Winter of the World, his citadel was attacked 
by possessed golems. He enacted a ritual that caused azurite to grow throughout the citadel,
and he became known as the Crystal King. He remains there, buried deep underground.
Ahkeli: (see The Order of the Djinn.)
MARAKETH
ANTIQUITY
Nekraata: a being that Maraketh fight after death in spiritual combat. No mortal has ever won.

- 466 -
DURING & AFTER THE WINTER OF THE WORLD
Khatal: a tale-man in the early years of the Winter of the World before the alliance (the Third 
Pact?) was forged. He had a unique gift for shaping water. His people were besieged and dying 
of thirst, and he managed to pull water from underground, saving his people. However, he 
turned to dust as a result.
Rashi: a woman bound to the first barya (and thus possibly the first Djinn). Unlike others bound to 
baryas, she wasn't a criminal but chose to be bound so she could serve as the Grand Water 
Djinn. Since then, she has fulfilled the sacred duty of collecting water from the winds and 
bleeding herself to replenish the reserves of water in the Qimah Reservoir.
Rangeen: a Djinn trapped in a barya. While human, Kulemak assaulted her caravan and she ran. 
The rest of her group died and were resurrected to serve the Lightless. It's implied Rangeen 
was imprisoned for cowardice/desertion, and her attitude is spiteful. She convinced the 
Serpent Clan to free her (but is interrupted by the player).
Varashta: the Winter Sekhema. She designed and oversaw the building of the proving grounds for 
the sisterhood (the Trial of Sekhemas) with Zarokh's help. Zarokh wanted to rule the Vastiri 
with her, but she didn't want this, so he turned on her and cursed the halls of the Trial. 
Varashta retaliated by trapping him as a Djinn in the farthest halls of the Trial, where aspirants 
don't need to go. However, because of his curse, Varashta was trapped there as well and can no 
longer survive outside the chamber. She believes she is trapped more in time than in space, due 
to Zarokh's powers.
Kelari: a man in Varashta's akhara who apparently loved Navira. During a war, he told Navira 
there were cowards among Ruzhan's ranks. Navira passed this on to Ruzhan, who killed them. 
Kelari then set a trap on their corpses, causing beetles to burst forth and halting, but not 
defeating, their enemy. Navira and Ruzhan both later testified that Kelari's claim about the 
cowards was a deception used to gain power. For his actions, Kelari was bound to a barya as a 
Djinn and became known as the Tainted Sands.
Navira: the Tale Woman of Varashta's akhara. During a war, Kelari told her there were cowards 
among Ruzhan's ranks. She passed this on to Ruzhan, who killed them. When facing 
consequences for her actions, Navira claimed Kelari had deceived her. Varashta bound her to a 
barya as a Djinn for condoning Kelari's and Ruzhan's actions, and she became known as the Last 
Mirage.
Ruzhan: a man in Varashta's akhara. During a war, Navira told him there were cowards among his 
ranks per Kelari. Ruzhan killed them with a sword and fire, believing their akhara could not 
tolerate weakness during a war. When facing consequences for his actions, he claimed Kelari 
had deceived him. However, he agreed to be bound to a barya as a Djinn for his actions, 
becoming known as the Blazing Sword.
Zarokh: a man who achieved great things in the war against the Lightless and helped build the Trial 
of Sekhemas. Varashta says he came to them a taljari, but became something more. His 
ambition grew and wanted to rule the Vastiri with Varashta, but she didn't, so he turned on her. 
He stole the wisdom of the tale-women and became the first Chronomancer, and cursed the 

- 467 -
halls of the Trial. Varashta retaliated by trapping him as a Djinn in the farthest halls of the Trial, 
where aspirants don't need to go. He claims to be able to see the past and foresee the future, 
though his foretellings aren't always correct.
Halani, Goddess of Water: a Maraketh woman who ascended to godhood. She had a son when she 
was still mortal, who she left to die (possibly because he was considered imperfect). She claims 
she was later told that he'd died, so after ascending to godhood didn't seek him out. After the 
Beast put her to sleep she dreamed of living happily with her son, but when she awoke in an 
abandoned Keth she was unable to move (and appears to have been mutilated/disemboweled). 
Keth’s second river was named after her, as were the Halani Gates that were once water-locks.
Azarian, the Forsaken Son: Halani's son, who she left to die. He lived with the Faridun for thirty 
years and says he had a harsh and painful life, while hating his mother for abandoning him. He 
was apparently resurrected by Corruption after the new Beast was brought to the Vastiri.
Solerai: a sekhema and the twin sister of Lundara. During the Winter of the World, she and her 
sister are said to have wielded the essence of gold and silver, clearing up the grey sky and 
causing the winter to end. She wielded a legendary spear, which was later lost or stolen and 
which has been sought out by various people throughout the ages. One of Orbala's adventures 
involved tracking down the spear. Some believe that Solerai may have been the same person as 
the Azmeri goddess Solaris.
Lundara: a sekhema and the twin sister of Solerai. During the Winter of the World, she and her 
sister are said to have wielded the essence of gold and silver, clearing up the grey sky and 
causing the winter to end. Some believe that Lundara may have been the same person as the 
Azmeri goddess Lunaris.
Balbala: a sekhema who betrayed her akhara for a promise of welakath, a mythical elixir said to 
bestow great power. She secretly led a band of foreign warriors to the top of the Halani Gates, 
where her akhara was slain to the last woman. Instead of rewarding her, the bandits put a 
spear through her gut. Death was considered insufficient punishment for her crime, and 
Balbala agreed to be imprisoned as a Djinn because she felt she deserved it. Her sentence was 
for one thousand years of suffering, but the location of her prison was later forgotten and she 
was left there much longer (by Zarka's reckoning, at least two or three thousand years). Balbala 
also says that even after her long imprisonment, her crimes will still not be forgiven until she 
successfully helps an aspirant through the Trial of the Sekhemas. She has scars on the left side 
of her face and may be blind her left eye.
Orbala, a.k.a. Garukhan, Queen of the Wind: a Maraketh woman famed for her eight adventures. 
One of these involved a hunt for Solerai’s Spear, which led her to Stridevolf and left it in flames. 
Another involved her having to impersonate a Vaal dignitary after killing a Maraketh spy who 
had in turn been impersonating a Vaal dignitary. This adventure left Lira Vaal in flames. Her 
eighth and last adventure began when she heard of the threat of the necromancer Saresh and 
set out on a quest to master the elements, resulting in the Horn of the Vastiri. She blew it and 
dissipated the sandstorms, allowing the united akharas to defeat Saresh. For this victory, 
Orbala was made the Sekhema of Sekhemas, and later became the Queen of the Wind, greatest 
goddess of the Maraketh. Her divine name was Garukhan, meaning "ultimate sovereign." Her 
war-steed was Ekbab the mastodon, and she wielded a sword called the Storm Blade, which 
was lost in the eastern desert during her battle against Saresh. Statues depict her as having had 

- 468 -
five sisters. She married the god Sin and they had a daughter, Shakari. Sin and Garukhan later 
parted ways, and he gives her as one reason he created the Beast and put the gods to sleep. Sin 
describes Garukhan as a prideful, stubborn, and vain woman who sought wisdom in the sky.
Shakari, Queen of the Sands: the daughter of Garukhan and Sin. As the daughter of two gods, it's 
possible that Shakari was born divine and didn't need to ascend on her own, though this isn't 
confirmed. Per Sin, she was envious of her mother’s power, and so sought power for herself,
finding it in the sand. He says she was driven by agony and shame and amassed her own army. 
It’s suggested that she intended to wage war on the sky (and thus her mother) but was stopped 
when the Beast put her to sleep.
DURING THE DECLINE & FALL OF THE ETERNAL EMPIRE
Asenath, the Golden Sekhema: the Maraketh sekhema and archer who united the Maraketh tribes 
against the Eternal Empire. She was the last person to bear the Wings of Vastiri, which 
bestowed her with the title of "Sekhema of Sekhemas." She led the united Maraketh against 
Sarn, but was defeated and killed by General Hector Titucius.
Deshret, the Red Sekhema: the commander who led the Maraketh during the Purity Rebellion. 
Voll promised her the return of the Maraketh grazing lands stolen during the imperial conquest 
of the Vastiri Plains in return for her military support in the rebellion. She agreed, and led her 
akhara in an attack against General Hector Titucius' legionnaires. They were successful, and 
Deshret is said to have fashioned a rhoa saddle from his skin. She later joined Voll for the siege 
of Sarn. Following the Cataclysm, she led her akhara to Highgate to stop the Beast. However, 
she instead chose to seal off the mines and order her akhara to guard them. She was later killed 
by Emperor Voll, who had been corrupted into a monster by the Cataclysm. After death her 
spirit fell into the hands of Malachai's Godless Three, who each had their wicked way with her, 
attempting to subsume her into the collective corruption. They failed, leaving her spirit trapped 
within the mines.
RECENT TIMES
Torbik: a travelling merchant who struck off on his own several years ago, without a caravan. He 
says it's tough but he likes the freedom. He plans to accumulate goods and take them to the 
Karui archipelago, because he's heard there's water there as far as the eye can see and wants to 
see it for himself. He hopes the Khari Bazaar will become a trade hub again like it was in 
ancient times. He has a rhex named Dabu.

- 469 -
THE KIYATO AKHARA
Oyun: the sekhema of the Kiyato akhara, which was charged by Deshret with guarding the Highgate 
mines. She successfully defended Highgate against the Ebony Legion attack led by Captain 
Vincenti, which had been ordered by Piety.
Kira: a dekhara of the Kiyato akhara, which was charged by Deshret with guarding the Highgate 
mines. She is a descendant of Deshret.
Tasuni: Kira's brother. He was born blind so was left out on the plain overnight as per Maraketh 
tradition. However, he survived (apparently on his own, without the help of the Faridun), 
which had never happened before. He claims to be an augur with the ability to see things others 
cannot.
Irasha: a dekhara of the Kiyato akhara and possible successor to Oyun. She had a twin sister who 
died during her dance with the scorpion. When Irasha was twelve, she was attacked by three 
men and possibly raped. They were later caught and she executed them herself.
THE ARDURA AKHARA
Asala: the sekhema of the Ardura akhara. Shambrin describes her as beautiful, strong, and cunning.
Zarka: the tale-woman of the Ardura akhara, who was chosen by her predecessor.
Shambrin: a dekhara in the Ardura akhara until blinded in battle. She still practices with a sword 
in the hope of fighting again (Nasima is her inspiration), but she now serves as tradesmith and 
weaponmaster for the Ardura. She's a bit sympathetic toward the Faridun given her own injury 
and experiences.
Lailuma: a woman who Shambrin cares about. She went to Deshar alone and threw herself from 
the spires. As she was not sick or injured at the time, her act was likely considered 
dishonourable. A possible reason for her suicide is hopelessness regarding being with 
Shambrin, which may have been forbidden by the Ardura.
UNKNOWN
Devora: a Djinn. She mentions a drought, but also boats, the Seven Waters, and Halani. Thus she 
may be from an earlier era when the Vastiri was still lush.
Razel: a Djinn who speaks of sand, and thus he may be from a more recent time when the Vastiri 
has desertified.
Yoon: a Djinn trapped in a barya. He is remorseful and feels he deserves his punishment. He wants 
to suffer and serve in order to be redeemed.

- 470 -
Amnaah: the third servant of water. It's possible Amnaah is the author of the final testament found 
in Keth, suggesting that he/she remained behind after the Beast was created and the city 
abandoned, hoping that Halani would awaken. Amnaah is referred to as the last Djinn, which 
may mean the last one to have been created.
Aziza: the fourth servant of water. A tale claims that Aziza is a Djinn who lives in a lamp.
Aukuna, the Black Sekhema: a Maraketh general who was skilled at both archery and hand-tohand combat. She rode a mount named Shiyo. She fought to defend Highgate against the risen 
dead, so may have been a sekhema of the Kiyato akhara before Oyun (and probably after the 
death of Deshret). Currently she resides in the Domain of Timeless Conflict and seems to 
believe she's still fighting the dead even when facing other human factions.
Nasima of the Second Sight: a woman born blind with red eyes, who was abandoned by the 
Maraketh for her imperfection. She was taken in by the Faridun and became a great warrior. 
One day, she was sent to raid the akhara that had abandoned her. While there she recognised 
her mother's voice, so turned on and began killing the Faridun. The Maraketh consider her a 
good role model. (The Brutal Restraint Timeless Jewel may imply that she became a sekhema.)
Wranga: a tale-woman of the Wahida akhara.
OUTCASTS (FARIDUN)
Saresh: (see The Order of the Djinn.)
Jamanra: a Faridun warrior who was alive during the time the gods were asleep. He believed the 
Faridun and Maraketh were equals, an idea the Maraketh saw as dangerous. He wanted to 
prove the Faridun were strong in order to convince the Maraketh that casting them out was a 
mistake, and to reunite with them, hoping to rebuild Keth together. (Per unused POE I lore, the 
Faridun consisted of scattered camps and he united them into a single people.) The Maraketh 
sekhemas joined together and met with him. Per them, he was in awe of their glory and killed 
himself, though even Zarka grows to doubt this account. (Per unused POE I lore, they'd agreed 
to meet with him to discuss recognising the Faridun as its own nation, but betrayed and 
poisoned him.) Jamanra was resurrected by Oriana using the new Beast. He was driven mad by 
Corruption and seeks to use the power of the Beast to get revenge against the Maraketh.
Nenet: (see The Ring.)
Risu: a woman who was left to die in the desert as an infant by the Maraketh and taken in by the 
Faridun. She has no idea who her mother or father are (they could be in the Ardura). She was 
horrified by the Beast Oriana brought to the Faridun and didn’t want to go to war against the 
Maraketh with Jamanra, so after the Dreadnought was complete Jamara sealed her and other 
dissenters in Mawdun Mine. There she was kept in a locked cage by Rudja.

- 471 -
Rudja, the Dread Engineer: a Faridun engineer who likely helped build Jamanra's Dreadnought. 
She was left behind in Mawdun Mine by Jamanra, possibly to deal with the dissenters. She 
appears to be undead, and was likely reanimated by Corruption.
L'im the Impaler: a spearwoman who is part of the forward command of the Faridun offensive 
against the Maraketh under Jamanra.
Azmadi: a Faridun who desired to become the Sekhema of Sekhemas. He completed the Trial of the 
Sekhemas (becoming the first Faridun to do so) with Zarokh's help. He was granted some of 
Zarokh's power over time in exchange for agreeing to help Zarokh escape by stealing the First 
Barya. He considers himself a prince of the Faridun.
VAAL
ANTIQUITY
Xibaqua: the precursor to the Vaal. Xibaqua was said to have been born from the flesh of the gods, 
but later betrayed them. The gods reclaimed their flesh, leaving nothing left of Xibaqua save for 
a droplet of pure light, which was the first Vaal.
Ralakesh, Master of a Million Faces: a Vaal god said to be obsessed with governance and the 
subjugation of humanity through their base, animal instincts. He conducted experiments that 
wiped out so many of his people that he had to enslave many primitive Azmeri in order to 
repopulate his domain. He had a terror of grasping too much and having it all slip through his 
fingers and therefore remained on his throne surrounded by high walls while other deities 
waged war and conquered empires.
Yugul, Reflection of Terror: a Vaal scholar. He was interested in human terror and would terrify 
children and capture their reactions in eldritch mirrors for study. He used what he learned to 
manipulate his way into a leadership position and eventually became so renowned that he 
ascended to godhood.
Arakaali, Spinner of Shadows: a prostitute with insatiable lust, who used her talents as a 
temptress and predator to rise to godhood. Per Cadiro she was worshipped by the Ameri 
before the Vaal, so may have actually been an Azmerian. She would sedate her victims, have her 
carnal way with them, and then drain them completely of all fluids. The children of Gruthkul 
became envious of Arakaali’s power and plotted against her, so Arakaali killed them. Gruthkul 
retaliated by attacking Arakaali’s realm and bringing it to the brink of ruin. Arakaali lured 
Gruthkul into a cavern and collapsed it on her, trapping Gruthkul inside. She then began 
rebuilding her empire, but the Beast was born and she began to weaken. Her followers then 
betrayed her, binding her in silk and leaving her trapped in a pyramid.

- 472 -
Kopec, the Sun God: the Vaal God of the Sun. His temple in Utzaal contained a time machine 
powered by an artificial sun, which was intended to be used to preserve the Vaal people in the 
event of a cataclysm.
Kamasa, the Monkey God: the Vaal Monkey God and Vaal God of Wealth. He was initially curious, 
wise, and prone to mischief. Tales of his early life depict him as appearing to impart mysterious 
wisdom or steal something shiny from a wealthy noble. However, his greed grew as the Vaal 
expanded, and later tales portray him extorting peasants and blackmailing nobles for 
increasingly large tithes. His cult's core values became exploitation and ambition, and his high 
priests eventually ran everything remotely financial in the Vaal Empire. He had a temple, vault, 
and forge in Utzaal.
Yaomac: a Vaal god represented as a three-headed snake. Yaomac is said to be the shepherd of 
Vaal souls and the arbiter of the balance of the seasons, and to have found unity in balance. 
Three unique blessings are supposed to be conferred by each of Yaomac's three serpentine 
heads. The Venom Crypts in the jungle outside of Utzaal are the remains of the Temple of 
Yaomac. Yaomac was kidnapped by Ixchel (who later became the Trialmaster) while asleep due 
to the influence of the Beast. Servi's dialogue hints that Yaomac is female.
Chaos: an unknown entity. Per the Trialmaster, moments of chance lead to multiple diverging 
paths of reality, and Chaos sees all of them. Chaos is fascinated by the ability of the skilled to 
bend chance in their favour, and has tasked the Trialmaster with finding challengers and 
putting them through trials of skill and chance. Per the Trialmaster, Atziri is an enigma because 
her life is the one event that never changes in any version of reality.
Ahuatotli, the Blind: the Grand Architect of the Vaal Outpost, a city which was eventually buried 
beneath the Eternal Empire.
Tetzlapokal: a Vaal queen sometimes referred to as a "waif of disturbing proclivities." She was a 
devotee of Arakaali and supposedly had a deep fascination with mortality and the inert human 
form. It was said she would request that her subjects deposit the bodies of their deceased loved 
ones upon the steps of her palace, to be taken inside and used for disturbing purposes.
DURING THE TIME OF THE BEAST
Ixchel, a.k.a. The Trialmaster: a being who was once a mortal man named Ixchel. His people went 
mad with fear after the gods went to sleep, and he was taken in by the Order of the Djinn. He 
infiltrated the Priesthood of Yaomac and kidnapped the sleeping god. The Order then sent him 
to do the same to Chaos, though Chaos was discovered awake (and thus not a god). Following 
this, Ixchel served Chaos and became known as the Trialmaster. He has been tasked with 
searching for suitable challengers for trials of skill and chance. He may also award titles to 
those who successfully complete the trials. Through Chaos, the Trialmaster experiences many 
different outcomes or versions of the same events. (Note that most of the above lore came from 
scarabs that have now been removed from the game.)

- 473 -
DURING THE REIGN OF ATZIRI
Atziri: the last queen of the Vaal. Inspired by Zerphi, she sought out youth and longevity at the cost 
of sacrificing her own people. Historical records state that Doryani orchestrated a communion 
with the Beast involving Virtue Gems and the harvest moon, hoping to achieve immortality for 
his people. However, Doryani claims it was Atziri who attempted the communion and that he 
tried but failed to stop her. In either case, the result was the Fall and the destruction of Vaal 
civilisation. While believed to have died in the Fall, she somehow remained behind in a 
nightmare realm that is beginning to leak back into Wraeclast. Per the Trialmaster, Atziri is an 
enigma because her life is the one event that never changes in any version of reality.
Zerphi: a Vaalish noble and infamous serial killer who tortured and murdered thirteen people. He 
lived to be 168, but at the time of his death had the body of a 20-year-old. This inspired Atziri in 
her pursuit of youth and longevity.
Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge, First Seer to the Queen: a Vaal thaumaturgist who served under 
Queen Atziri. He was patroned by Chaos, who took an interest in him after his strategy in the 
Trial of Chaos greatly amused Chaos. Doryani assisted Atziri in her pursuit of youth and 
longevity at the cost of human sacrifice and experimentation. As part of this, he studied biology, 
machinery, Corruption, time, and other fields. He considered the study of the Beast to be his 
life's work and saw it as the means to achieve his goals. He disregarded any ethical boundaries 
and there was at least one attempt on his life. Historical records state that he orchestrated 
some sort of communion with the Beast involving Virtue Gems and the harvest moon, hoping to 
achieve immortality for his people, and per Sin he wounded the Beast. However, Doryani 
himself claims it was Atziri who attempted the communion and that he tried but failed to stop 
her, going so far as to make contingency plans in case the communion was catastrophic. In 
either case, the result was the Fall and the destruction of Vaal civilisation.
Viper Napuatzi: a woman who was taken as an unwilling sacrifice, but her blood was refused. She 
later rose to become a Vaal general, becoming known as the Fang of the Vaal and her troops as 
the Viper Legionnaires. In battle she used poison-based spells and had the ability to summon 
spectral snakes. She lived in Utzaal. After being defeated (by the player) shortly before the Fall 
of the Vaal, she was somehow transported to the Domain of Timeless Conflict.
Nezahul: a Royal Commander under Viper Napuatzi.
Ketzuli, High Priest of the Sun & Architect of Time: a Vaal architect who studied time, 
conducting his research in the Temple of Kopec. His writings are still extant. He believed that 
time is solid and cannot be changed, and thus travelling to the past won't affect what happens in 
the future. He considered Doryani to be the greatest hero of their era, and hoped to give him 
the time he needed to complete his work.
Atalui: a blood priestess and Atazek's twin sister.
Atazek: a blood priest and Atalui's twin brother.

- 474 -
Kishara: a Vaal sailor said to have explored every coast, cove and bay of Wraeclast. She was aided 
by the Star, an artefact she obtained on her first voyage that guided her wherever she wanted to 
go. She had seventeen children and was renowned for manning the helm while pregnant and 
even giving birth during battles more than once. Her children went on to found the Brinerot
warband. There are stories and songs of her visiting Phaaryl and the Viridian Wildwood, and 
the Maraketh claim she was captain of a Maraketh merchant vessel. Supposedly, she sailed to 
Middengard on her last voyage and Queen Atziri didn't like the attention she was getting, so 
impounded everything Kishara brought back and made sacrifices of her crew. For her feats, 
Kishara was known as the Southern Star and the Wayward Gull.
Jaetai: a Vaal Queen's Advisor, including advisor to Queen Atziri (per Cadiro).
Ichlotl the Blackjaw: a notorious criminal who was imprisoned in a Soul Core for his crimes. He 
sparked the first rumours that those who were sacrificed remained aware inside their Soul 
Cores. The construct powered by his Soul Core was excessively violent when given the chance 
and seemed to display anger when in combat. The Vaal considered this a plus, and set him to 
guard the Machinarium where Soul Cores were manufactured.
Zicoatl, Warden of the Core: the most advanced construct ever built by the Vaal, powered by a 
large Soul Core. It was built into the structure of Jiquani's Machinarium itself and set to activate 
if interlopers ever infiltrated the heart of the facility, in order to protect the Machinarium's 
secrets. (Zicoatl is spelled "Zicoati" in the book The Art of Path of Exile II.)
Anub, the Pinata: a woman who was part scorpion and resided with the garrison in Atziri's Temple 
in Lira Vaal.
Coztic, the Forgehand: a man in Atziri's Temple in Lira Vaal who used a large hammer.
Cualli, Kamasan Smith: a male smith in Atziri's Temple in Lira Vaal.
Huitzil, Royal Blood Priest: a male priest in the Sacrificial Chamber in Atziri's Temple in Lira Vaal.
Kulka, Vaal Thaumaturge: a male thaumaturge in Atziri's Temple in Lira Vaal.
Menmek, Guardian Construct: a Soul Core-powered construct in the Alchemy Lab in Atziri's 
Temple in Lira Vaal.
Micata, the Remade: a woman in Atziri's Temple in Lira Vaal. She is part machine.
Pakteni, Flesh Surgeon: a doctor in Atziri's Temple in Lira Vaal. He was taught by Guatelitzi.
Temoc, Drill Overseer: a male solider who was part of the garrison in Atziri's Temple in Lira Vaal.
Xalapa, Spy Master: a spymaster in Atziri's Temple in Lira Vaal. She wielded claws.
Xolotl, Royal Commander: a commander who resides in Atziri's Temple in Lira Vaal. He wields a 
large axe. He was human during the Fall of the Vaal but in the present appears to occupy a Soul 
Core in a stone construct and has become known as Xolotl, the Forgotten.

- 475 -
ARCHITECTS
Xipocado, Royal Architect: an architect who designed the Royal Meeting Room, Hall of Lords, and 
Throne of Atziri in Atzoatl. Atziri was impressed when he openly spoke his mind about her and 
made him her personal architect. He rebuilt Lira Vaal, including designing a personal temple for 
Atziri that he described as "a living machine" able to modify its internal structure. He was 
precise, scientific, and calculated, and a devout adherent of Atziri.
Ahuana, Architect of Ceremonies: an architect who led countless human sacrifices. He designed 
the Sacrificial Chamber, Hall of Offerings, and Apex of Ascension in Atzoatl. (Note that there 
was also a Karui queen named Ahuana, who lived well over a thousand years later.)
Atmohua, Architect of Iron: a male architect who designed the Armourer's Workshop, Armoury, 
and Chamber of Iron in Atzoatl.
Azcapa, Architect of the Guild: an architect and notoriously talented jeweler. He designed the 
Jeweller's Workshop, Jewellery Forge, and Glittering Halls in Atzoatl. He had quarters in Utzaal.
Cholotl, Architect of the War: a male architect who designed the Guardhouse, Barracks, and Hall 
of War in Atzoatl.
Citaqualotl, Architect of the Swarm: an architect and crazed scientist who created moving devices 
of strange metals and later combined metal and insects. He designed the Hatchery, Automaton 
Lab, and Hybridisation Chamber in Atzoatl.
Estazunti, Architect of the Vault: a male architect who designed the Vault, Treasury, and Wealth 
of the Vaal in Atzoatl.
Guatelitzi, Architect of Flesh: a boy who was found moving among the prisoners, "preparing"
(mutilating) their living bodies for sacrifice. The high priests recognised his inclinations and 
gave him a higher calling as an architect. He designed the Pools of Restoration, Sanctum of 
Vitality, and Sanctum of Immortality in Atzoatl.
Hayoxi, Architect of Destruction: an architect who designed the Explosives Room, Demolition 
Lab, and Shrine of Unmaking in Atzoatl. In Lira Vaal, he built up a pile of powder under the 
royal temple but never had the courage to light it. He committed suicide by blowing himself up, 
but Atziri had has body reassembled.
Jiquani, Architect of Industry: an architect obsessed with finding new and creative ways to get 
things done. He was the mastermind behind making constructs of stone animated by Soul Cores 
in order to help his people keep pace with their own rapid expansion. In order to achieve this, 
he sacrificed countless peasants, and some say their screams still echo inside their Soul Cores. 
He had his own machinarium near Utzaal. He also designed the Workshop, Engineering 
Department, and Factory in Atzoatl.
Juatalotli, Architect of the Hoard: an architect who designed the Storage Room, Warehouses, and 
Museum of Artefacts in Atzoatl. He gathered every piece of Vaal history he could, hoping to 
preserve them. He also obtained ancient and notable relics through trade, excavation, and 
raids. The elders from the Huntress player character's village gave him some sacred objects for 
preservation. He had a hoard of such objects in Atziri's Temple in Lira Vaal.

- 476 -
Matatl, Architect of Fortifications: a male architect who designed the Trap Workshop, Temple 
Defense Workshop, and Defense Research Lab in Atzoatl.
Opiloti, Architect of Strife: an architect and brutally violent warlord. He used to spill the blood of 
his greatest warriors, believing it would grant them immortality. He designed the Hall of 
Champions, Hall of Heroes, and Hall of Legends in Atzoatl.
Paquate, Architect of Corruption: an architect who performed nefarious experiments. He built a 
corruption mechanism in Jiquani's Sanctum, and also designed the Corruption Chamber, 
Catalyst of Corruption, and Locus of Corruption in Atzoatl. He also built the Locus of Corruption 
in Atziri's Temple in Lira Vaal.
Puhuarte, Architect of the Forge: a Vaal architect who designed the Flame Workshop, Omnitect 
Forge, and Crucible of Flame in Atzoatl.
Quipolatl, Architect of the Nexus: an architect who proposed building the Temple of Atzoatl as a 
prototype. There, he designed the Shrine of Empowerment, Sanctum of Unity, and Temple 
Nexus.
Tacati, Architect of Toxins: a male architect who designed the Poison Garden, Cultivar Chamber, 
and Toxic Grove in Atzoatl. He attempted to assassinate Atziri with a unique poison, but it 
required him to direct his anger to be effective and in her presence he could only feel lust.
Ticaba, Architect of the Arena: a male architect who designed the Sparring Room, Arena of 
Valour, and Hall of Champions in Atzoatl.
Topotante, Architect of Storms: an architect who designed the Tempest Generator, Hurricane 
Engine, and Storm of Corruption in Atzoatl.
Tzamoto, Architect of Torment: a male architect who designed the Torment Cells, Torture Cages, 
and Sadist's Den in Atzoatl.
Uromoti, Architect of Expansion: an architect who designed the Surveyor's Study, Office of 
Cartography, and Atlas of Worlds in Atzoatl. He had quarters in Utzaal. He went to the Azmeri 
and asked to buy Mount Kriar from them, but the Azmeri didn't understand the concept of 
owning a mountain so just let the Vaal pass. He built the Cuachic Vault and sent his children 
there, before returning to Atzoatl to play his part and placate Atziri.
Xopec, Architect of Power: an architect who experimented into electrical lifebloods. He designed 
the Lightning Workshop, Omnitect Reactor Plant, and Conduit of Lightning in Atzoatl.
Zalatl, Architect of Thaumaturgy: an architect who designed the Gemcutter's Workshop, 
Department of Thaumaturgy, and Doryani's Institute in Atzoatl.
Zantipi, Architect of Concealment: a male architect who designed the Strongbox Chamber, Hall of 
Locks, and Court of Sealed Death in Atzoatl.
Zilquapa, Architect of the Breach: a male architect who designed the Splinter Research Lab, 
Breach Containment Chamber, and House of the Others in Atzoatl.

- 477 -
RECENT TIMES
The Last to Die: the last survivor of the bloodlines of the High Priests of the Vaal. During the height 
of the Vaal empire's madness, the Blood Crucible was forged as part of a pact between the High 
Priests and the entity known as Chaos. For most of her life, The Last to Die has used the Blood 
Crucible to shift into Nightmare and fight the Scourge, three factions of horrific creatures, 
though says she's accomplished nothing but outliving everyone else. She implies she's seen 
countless different versions of Wraeclast, and that all were destroyed by the Scourge except 
one, which was dominated by High Templar Venarius. Per Divinia, she mysteriously 
disappeared from a Templar jail cell a few years before encountering the exile. It is very likely 
that The Last to Die is actually Alva Valai from an alternate Wraeclast.
Zelina: a blood priestess and current head of the Cuachic Vault with her twin brother Zolin. She 
used excess newborns in the vault to scry for dreams.
Zolin: a blood priest and current head of the Cuachic Vault with his twin sister Zelina.
Stormgore, the Guardian: like Blackjaw, Storegore was a soul trapped in a Soul Core within a 
stone body, and was stationed as a guard at the entrance to the Cuachic Vault.
TRIBES REMAINING AFTER THE FALL
CENOBITES & ANCHORITES
The Queen of Filth: queen of the degenerated Vaal who remain in the flooded city of Utzaal. She 
resides at the top of Aggorat, surrounded by poisonous waters, and refers to outsiders as 
"cleanskins." Like the other survivors, she is a cannibal--who prefers to eat her victims alive--
and implies that she's eaten members of her own family. She practices inbreeding and has 
multiple sons. She despises the Karui enough to refuse to eat them. She loves gold.
Cauldron Keeper: the gentle crone, who will give out flasks in exchange for the right mushrooms.
Mektul, the Forgemaster: the forgemaster in Kamasa's Molten Vault.
SERVI’S UNNAMED TRIBE
Servi: a guide from a tribe that's lived near Utzaal for generations. She's paid handsomely by 
treasure hunters to provide local knowledge and warn them about which plants, animals, and 
other dangers to avoid. She uses charms, says ritualistic phrases, and makes small sacrifices at 
idols. She has a son and a grandson (Apus), and describes them both and having a rowdy spirit. 
She says her tribe's darkest tales feature Doryani.
Apus: Servi's grandson, who she describes as having a rowdy spirit.

- 478 -
OROKS (AZAKH-KUL)
Ranbu the Pale Shaman: a female Orok Shaman.
Garkam, Ranbu's Maul: a male Orok giant.
AZAKS (CARVERS)
Ignagduk, the Bog Witch: the queen-witch of the Azak tribe. On the night of each blood moon, she
steals a child from the local tribes and sacrifices it in a bloody ritual, causing his/her soul to 
serve her forever afterwards. Capable of horrific dark magic, Ignagduk is known as the 
deadliest witch in the jungle. She wields a spear adorned with the skulls of children.
Narag: a female shaman with a hut in the Matlan Waterways.
UNKNOWN
Ixtolatl, Artisan of Sacrifice: guardian of the Gifts of the Sacrificed Vaal Reliquary.
Mahuatzi, Artisan of Desire: guardian of the Gifts of the Red Queen Vaal Reliquary.
Zeel: a Vaal tinkerer in search of the secret of Matter Metamorphosis.
Mahuxotl: a banished architect who sought to employ the darkest secrets of the Vaal.
Kiravi: a Vaal archer.
KARUI
ANTIQUITY
Tukohama, Father of War: a Karui god who's considered responsible for transforming the Karui 
from a peaceful culture of farers and fisherman into warriors with a hunger for conquest. 
Tukohama's tribe was in continual conflict with the Ngamahu tribe, so to put an end to it 
Tukohama and Ngamahu went through the traditions together, and she gave her ring to him. 
It's said that Tukohama went to war against the First Ones of the Ezomytes.

- 479 -
Ngamahu, Mother of Fire: a Karui goddess. Ngamahu's tribe was in continual conflict with the 
Tukohama tribe, so to put an end to it Ngamahu and Tukohama went through the traditions 
together, and he helped her forge her legendary axe.
Valako, Father of the Storm: a Karui god.
Tasalio, Father of Water: a Karui god.
Sione, Mother of the Sun: the Karui goddess of the Sun. Tales say that in the past, the Sun was 
green and no brighter than any other star. Sione traded away all of her tribe's possessions to 
foreign cultures in exchange for gold, and plated her palace with it. Her tribe was on the verge 
of starvation due to this, but put on a festival with what little they had left. Ramako was invited, 
and was so in awe of Sione's wealth that he agreed to go through the traditions together. His 
light was reflected by her gold palace, making the Sun what it is today and creating Day. This 
resulted in her tribe flourishing. Some claim that Ramako later had an affair with her sister, 
Lani Hua, and may be the father of her daughter, though Ramako denies this. Because of this, 
Sione went into the night sky to wage war on her sister. However, some claim that the sisters 
then discovered something so horrible that it drives even the strongest warriors to madness, 
and that since then the two sisters have been out protecting the rest of humanity by waging war 
with the stars themselves. Warriors wounded in this battle are tended to by Arohongui until 
well enough to rejoin the fight.
Lani Hua, Mother of the Moon: a Karui goddess and the sister of Sione. Arohongui is her daughter, 
who some claim is the product of an affair between Lani Hua and Ramako, her sister's husband, 
though Ramako denies this. Because of this, Sione went into the night sky to wage war on Lani 
Hua. However, some claim that the sisters then discovered something so horrible that it drives 
even the strongest warriors to madness, and that since then the two sisters have been out 
protecting the rest of humanity by waging war with the stars themselves. Warriors wounded in 
this battle are tended to by Arohongui until well enough to rejoin the fight.
Ramako, Father of Light, Father of the Sun: a Karui god. He was originally the Father of Light, 
but after being invited to a festival put on by Sione, he was in awe of her wealth and went 
through the traditions with her. Her golden palace reflected his light, making the Sun what it is 
today and earning Ramako the second title of Father of the Sun. Some believe that he secretly 
can't stand her, and asked his bother, Rongokurai, to provide darkness so that he could carry 
out an affair with Lani Hua, fathering her daughter, Arohongui. However, Ramako claims it was 
someone else who was visiting Lani Hua, and that Rongokurai is a liar. Because of this, he and 
his brother no longer speak. The Ramako tribe believe that a deceiver impersonated him and 
fathered Arohongui, before later being caught and locked away.
Rongokurai, Father of Night: a Karui god who hides and protects the innocent and brings relief 
from the heat of the day. Ramako is his brother. Some believe that Rongokurai provided 
darkness to hide Ramako while he carried on an affair with Lani Hua, though Ramako claims it 
was someone else who was with her and that Rongokurai is a liar. Because of this, Rongokurai 
and Ramako are no longer on speaking terms.
Arohongui, Daughter of the Moon: the daughter of Lani Hua. As the child of a goddess, she was 
born divine and thus can act as she pleases without the need of an agenda or accumulating 
loyalty. Some claim that her father is Ramako, though he denies this. The Ramako tribe believe 

- 480 -
that a deceiver impersonated him and fathered Arohongui, before later being caught and locked 
away. While Sione and Lani Hua are out waging war, Arohongui tends to warriors wounded in 
the conflict until well enough to rejoin the fight.
Tawhoa, Father and Son of the Forest: a Karui god said to gift humanity with the trees and birds 
so that they can enjoy beauty and peace. He's also said to have gifted Ironwood to one Karui 
tribe, as an alternative to jade which was in limited supply. He has a perspective of ages and 
thus stands aside from such things as wars. He has a desire to teach, and supposedly gave 
humans the ability to dream.
Kitava, Father of Chaos: a Karui god representing the primal desire of hunger. Because he was 
unable to stop consuming things, he was punished by his fellow gods. Tukohama cut a large 
bleeding X on his face, leaving him blind. Valako impaled Kitava with his jawbone. Finally, 
Hinekora whipped him with her hair, driving him into the darkness of her island (possibly the 
Halls of the Dead) to suffer for time beyond measure. Another story says that Hinekora bound 
him to a rock to trap him. The Karui also know him by other names, including the Black Spirit, 
the Cannibal King, and the Ravenous One.
Hinekora, Mother of Death: a Karui goddess who cares for the souls of the Karui after death. 
Before her, the dead simply ceased to exist. She created the Halls of the Dead, where their souls 
can go after death to lend their wisdom and strength to future generations. After some Karui 
were on the verge of madness after being there too long, she devised trials of mock warfare to 
keep them engaged. Hinekora serves Order and works to ensure that what must happen, 
happens. She is opposed to Chaos, who takes amusement in unlikelihoods and surprising 
events. She can't see the future, but can see some of the past and thereby predict what will 
probably happen again.
Kahuturoa: a man who lived thousands of years ago, when the Vaal were a massive empire and the 
Karui and Azmeri were friends. Currently he is the oldest soul in the Halls of the Dead, and 
doesn't enjoy fighting but is good at it. He's grown lethargic and forlorn due to the length of his 
existence there, and wishes he could see the Chambers of the Dishonoured. It's implied he was 
in a relationship with Rakiata. He is currently a member of the Rongokurai Tribe.
Hikatomanga: a man with a family who is said to have cheated the gods, and against whom 
Tukohama sought retribution.
DURING THE TIME OF THE BEAST
Maata: a man who lived some time after Kahuturoa. He was a peacemaker and diplomat who 
maintained relations with the Vaal to protect the Karui from the blood fever caused by the 
gems. He now resides in the Halls of the Dead, where he looks old, apparently because that's 
how he sees himself. Currently he's a member of the Tawhoa Tribe.

- 481 -
DURING THE DECLINE & FALL OF THE ETERNAL EMPIRE
Kiloava: a man who became chieftain of the Valako Tribe. When he inherited the tribe's signet, "it 
surged with the power of the storm," which it had never done before. He therefore appointed 
himself as "the Herald of War," and claims to have laid the foundation for Karui unification, 
before Kaom killed him at the age of 74 as part of said unification. Some claim his bloodline 
ended with him, but he actually had many children. He was delighted to awake in the Halls of 
the Dead in his prime, and is energetic and virile. He attempted to court Ikiaho but was turned 
down, though says he's "gone through the traditions" with everyone else there and that "if it 
moves, I'll chase it!" He remains a member of the Valako Tribe.
Akoya: a Karui woman who was killed by Kaom after a day-long fight with him, as part of his 
campaign to unite the Karui tribes. The passing of the years in the Halls of the Dead weighs 
heavily on her, and she hopes for the end of Time. She takes traditions and the Karui Way 
seriously. She was apparently a member of the Ngamahu Tribe when she was alive, as she'd 
received the goddess' sign, but is currently a member of the Tukohama Tribe. She is sometimes 
referred to as the Chainbreaker.
Akayo: a male Karui who was decapitated by Kaom during his campaign to unite the Karui tribes.
Rakiata: a chieftain whose tribe was attacked by Eternals looking for a fabled spear when she was 
13. Her chieftain and father were killed, and she hid the spear piece they had with Tasalio (who 
was presumably asleep). She found a ring that washed up on the shore and believed to be a gift 
from Tasalio. Per her, it had great power but she never used it. She was killed when Kaom cut 
off her head and hand during his campaign to unite the Karui tribes. She doesn't follow the 
Way, but has her own style, which she calls the Flow. Because of this, many other chieftains 
were hostile to her when she arrived in the Halls of the Dead, but Ikiaho defended her. It's 
implied she was in relationships with Kahuturoa and Kiloava. Currently she's a member of the 
Tasalio Tribe.
Kaom: the leader of the Karui during the Purity Rebellion. Voll recruited him into the rebellion, 
promising him Karui freedom in return for war. He united the Karui tribes by killing the 
weakest tribe leaders one by one until the others joined his cause. He led them in a successful 
invasion of Wraeclast, defeating Marceus Lioneye and his legion on the southern coast. Kaom 
cleansed the area of all Eternal citizens, including killing the women and children, and declared 
himself king of a new Karui kingdom in Wraeclast. He also intended to invade and conquer 
Oriath, as had been agreed upon with Voll. However, Kaom's new kingdom was devastated by 
the Cataclysm, causing the dead to rise and the animals to attack the living. He had a vision 
leading him to take his bravest 500 warriors north to Highgate and descend into the mountain 
to put an end to the Cataclysm. However, he became corrupted by Malachai's influence and 
went mad, killing his own 500 men. From then on he remained trapped in his own dream 
within the mountain. When he was finally killed, he was honoured with a place in the Halls of 
the Dead. When he arrived there he pursued Ikiaho because he'd heard she'd refused all the 
others, but she refused him too. He is currently a member of the Ngamahu Tribe, though was 
possibly a member of the Tukohama Tribe in life.

- 482 -
Lavianga Ngamako: a hatungo and Guardian of the Karui Way, who acted as Kaom's advisor. He 
was present for the Karui invasion of Wraeclast, though remained behind when Kaom took his 
500 warriors north to Highgate. When Kaom did not return, Hyrri led the Karui, including 
Lavianga, back to their native Ngamakanui. Lavianga is the author of the carvings along the 
coast chronicling the invasion and its aftermath.
Hyrri Ngamaku: Kaom's niece. Prior to the Karui invasion of Wraeclast, she traveled to Thebrus 
and studied archery with Voll's finest military tutors. Sources disagree on whether this was at 
Kaom's behest or whether he was unaware and furious when he found out. Marceus Lioneye 
believed the Karui laws forbade the use of archers, not knowing this prohibition did not extend 
to women or to Hyrri's tribe, the Ramako Tribe. Thus he was unprepared for the attack by 
Hyrri's archers, and his legionnaires were defeated. She later joined Voll for the siege of Sarn, 
where she commanded the Karui forces. She had a relationship with Victario Nevalius, and they 
had a daughter together named Ahuana, who was born before the Cataclysm. Victario gifted her 
a signed copy of "O' Eternal" with the inscription, "To my Karui Queen, The Ngamakanui rose 
has never been so beautiful nor its thorns so deadly. Let your aim never waver, and your story 
ever be told." After the Cataclysm devastated her people and Kaom left for Highgate without 
returning, Hyrri led her remaining people back to Ngamakanui. There she held the title of 
queen of the still-united Karui tribes, until leaving to take an army to deal with a strange threat 
on the edge of Ngamakanui. She never returned, and was later discovered in the Domain of 
Timeless Conflict (thus never making it to the Karui Halls of the Dead), where she seems to 
think she's fighting against slavers. Despite the prohibition of archers by the Karui not 
technically applying to her, she is still sometimes referred to as the Dishonoured Queen.
Ahuana: the daughter of Hyrri Ngamaku and Victario Nevalius, who was born shortly before the 
Cataclysm. She became queen of the still-united Karui tribes after Hyrri left to deal with a 
strange threat and never returned, but the tribes fractured. Ahuana suggested they switch to a 
council of chieftains, which remains to this day. She died in childbirth and now resides 
cheerfully in the Halls of the Dead with her descendants. Currently she's a member of the 
Ramako Tribe. (Note that one of the Vaal architects of Atzoatl was also named Ahuana, but was 
a man who lived well over a thousand years earlier.)
Siosa Foaga: a Karui slave of the Eternal Empire during the Purity Rebellion who apparently 
survived the Cataclysm due to being bound to a painting by a Karui motiata. He still resides in 
the Sarn library.
RECENT TIMES
Hapihapi: a man who helped the formerly-enslaved Karui refugees who'd escaped from Oriath 
after Kitava's rebirth settle into new lives in Wraeclast. He was captured and killed by slave 
traders, who were furious about the fall of the slave trading business and sought revenge by 
hunting down, torturing, and murdering as many Karui as they could find.
Tavakai: chieftain of the Tukohama Tribe and Makoru's father. He's known to be stubborn and a 
strict adherent to tradition. He sees the recent arrival of the Kalguurans as a threat to the Karui 

- 483 -
way of life and wants to unite the tribes to put the Karui first and make outsiders acknowledge 
their strength. Many Karui have been lost to foreign causes (the Kalguur and the Twilight 
Order) so he closed off Ngakanu to outsiders. He appealed to Tukohama and the other 
Ancestors for guidance. The earth rumbled and his axe glowed, causing him and others to 
believe he is the true leader of the Karui and to be followed without question. (In The Art of 
Path of Exile II his name is Hoko.)
Makoru: a woman who ran away from home (Ngakanu) to forge her own path rather than follow 
the strict traditions of the Karui Way. She joined the Kalguuran trade guild based in 
Kingsmarch as a deckhand. She later passed the test given by the Kalguur (the Captain's 
Challenge) with a unanimous vote, so was given command of a galleon named the Aurora May, 
becoming the first Karui captain on a Kalguuran ship. Her crew gathers what resources and 
artefacts they can and sends them back home in exchange for a cut of the profit. Her name 
means "shark" in Karui. Her father is Tavakai and she disagrees with him closing off the Karui 
to the outside world.
Kanu: first mate on the Aurora May. His family was from the Tasalio tribe but switched to the 
Tukohama tribe for their strength after the Kalguurans arrived. Growing up, he always liked to 
explore the waters and fish. He's said to be headstrong and loud, though had too many 
"modern" ideas for Tavakai's liking. He doesn't necessarily reject the Karui Way but disagrees 
with Tavakai's isolationist beliefs. He left his tribe before he was old enough to visit the Isle of 
Shrikes, and per Tavakai his father is ashamed. He is new to Kingsmarch.
Matiki: an Elder of the Tukohama tribe in Ngakanu. He became an Elder during the worst plague of 
Blood Fever the island had ever seen and gave of himself without a care. He is brave and wise 
per Kaimana. He's implied to have been with a woman named Rakana, who died. One day he 
took his canoe out and was deceived by a mysterious fog into thinking he saw Rakana. He 
followed her and crashed, ending up being held prisoner in a cage.
Rakana: a woman who Matiki says was sweet and strong. She's implied to have gone through the 
traditions with him but is now deceased.
Kaimana: Medicine Woman of the Tukohama Tribe. She calls herself a mystic, mother, doctor, 
protector, and follower.
Ruhaki: an apprentice carver on Ngakanu who is eager to trade for gold. He's tired of Tavakai's 
teachings and is interested in a future, not strength.
Harano, the Meat Carver: a Karui butcher of the Tukohama tribe.
UNKNOWN
Navali: a Karui hatungo from "long ago." In the Halls of the Dead, she fought for the Hinekora Tribe 
before apparently being replaced by Tawhanuku. Currently she remains there and serves 
Hinekora as "an interpreter of death and servant of prophecy." (In Prophecy League, Navali 
said she was greeted in the afterlife by her furry companion, Yama the White, holding a Seeing 

- 484 -
Stone. Yama and the Seeing Stone were both imbued with a hair of Hinekora's dark knowledge, 
allowing them to guide Navali through visions of the future. She then came back to life in 
Wraeclast, where she was captured by the Faun in what she believed was a trick by Hinekora to 
remind her of her place. In Trial of the Ancestors League, Yama is gone and this storyline seems 
to have been removed.)
Tawhanuku: a woman who's been in the Halls of the Dead for an unknown length of time. Not 
much is known about her life, as she is cryptic and speaks in fables. She's currently a member 
of the Hinekora Tribe.
Ikiaho: a woman who's been in the Halls of the Dead for an unknown length of time. She enjoys 
fighting but refuses to participate in other traditions, saying they aren't her culture. She's 
fascinated by the pursuit of knowledge and says that in life this pursuit led her to "a vast lake"
(possibly the Lake where Kalandra is trapped) but that she doesn't remember what she found 
there. She says that she doesn't know what love is and has spent her time in the Halls alone, 
declining to start a relationship with anyone. She is friends with Rakiata and feels understood 
by her. Currently she's a member of the Arohongui Tribe.
Oba: the Conqueror of Corruption.
AZMERI
ANTIQUITY
The Draíocht: a being or force with a mysterious nature. It's said that the Draíocht was originally a 
goddess, whose name has been forgotten. She had three aspects, known as the Three Sisters: 
the Mhacha, the Catha, and the Mórrigan. They sacrificed themselves to imbue every part of 
nature, living or not, with some of their essence. The result of this was the Draíocht.
The Mhacha: one of the three aspects of the Draíocht, also known as the Three Sisters. The Mhacha 
represented nature itself and was the one who convinced the sisters to sacrifice themselves to 
imbue every part of nature with some of their essence, resulting in the Draíocht.
The Catha: one of the three aspects of the Draíocht, also known as the Three Sisters. The Catha was 
said to be "the eternal battlefield betwixt good and evil" and represented the balance of 
opposites and that there is always hope. With her sisters, she sacrificed herself to imbue every 
part of nature with some of her essence, resulting in the Draíocht.
The Mórrigan: one of the three aspects of the Draíocht, also known as the Three Sisters. The 
Mórrigan was said to be a guide, representing bravery and the call to battle, and showed her 
people the way. With her sisters, she sacrificed herself to imbue every part of nature with some 
of her essence, resulting in the Draíocht.

- 485 -
Solaris, Eternal Sun: an Azmeri woman who ascended to godhood with her sister Lunaris. They 
lived together peacefully until the trickster Tangmazu captured Solaris, who believed her sister 
was responsible. This resulted in the two sisters being in endless conflict with each other. She's 
believed to represent various concepts including judgment, leadership, enlightenment, and 
belief. The Eternals considered her to be the right eye of their god.
Lunaris, Eternal Moon: an Azmeri woman who bathed her sick son in the ocean, killing him. She 
was put on trial by her tribe, and her sister Solaris tried to defend her, but she refused to admit 
any wrongdoing, saying that he was now safe beneath the dirt. She ascended to godhood with 
her sister, and they lived together peacefully until the trickster Tangmazu captured Solaris, who 
believed her sister was responsible. This resulted in the two sisters being in endless conflict 
with each other. She's believed to represent various concepts including mercy, dreams, 
inspiration, and wisdom. The Eternals considered her to be the left eye of their god.
Viridi: the sister of Solaris and Lunaris. It's likely that she was also a goddess, and had power 
related to nature and growth. Per the Azmeri creation myth, she appears to have been trapped 
inside the earth, and Solaris and Lunaris were unable to free her. It's also said that she was 
humble, in contrast to her sisters.
Prospero, Lord of the Underworld: the Azmeri god of the underworld and all treasures and 
substances that come from the earth. He's also the god of lost souls. Miners sometimes leave 
him tributes, and he's been known to make deals with people in exchange for riches or life. 
Cadiro claims to have located and made a deal with Prospero that has sustained him for three 
centuries. This would've occurred during the time of the Beast, and it's currently unknown how 
Prospero was able to have some cognizance and influence while the other gods were asleep.
Ryslatha, the Puppet Mistress: the Azmeri goddess of motherhood. She was once the matriarch of 
a peaceful and fertile tribe, until Tukohama swept through her lands and her people were 
butchered by war. She then vowed to make sure no one harmed her people again, by making 
everyone her people. She ascended to godhood and produced countless mindless offspring, to 
the point where the Azmeri feared that the world would collapse under the weight of them.
Tsoagoth, the Brine King: an Azmeri god. He was the beloved leader of a prosperous and 
sprawling seafarer tribe. However, he was unable to produce viable offspring to inherit his 
kingdom, which drove him to madness. After he ascended to godhood, sailors would often
whisper a prayer to him before casting off, and under a full moon the more superstitious 
captains would drown a slave or failed mutineer to keep him happy. He ruled over the city of 
Tsoatha, and when the Beast put him to sleep, he sank into the ocean and the city sank with 
him.
Thruldana: an unknown Azmeri god or goddess.
Kulric: a faithful follower of Solaris. When the goddess was imprisoned beneath the earth and 
tortured, he set her free and tended to her wounds.
Kulina: the last faithful follower of Lunaris. After the goddess was imprisoned and tortured by her 
sister, Kulina set her free and later urged her to go to war against Solaris.
Oisín: the first Warden of Eaves.

- 486 -
RECENT TIMES
Greust: an Azmerian who resided in the Forest Encampment atop the dam in the Phrecian Forest.
Silk: an Azmerian warrior who resided in the Forest Encampment atop the dam in the Phrecian 
Forest.
Yeena: an Azmerian who resided in the Forest Encampment atop the dam in the Phrecian Forest. 
She served a god or entity she called the Spirit, which gave her knowledge of events beyond 
what she and others saw themselves as well as the ability to shapeshift into a fox.
Oshabi: an Azmeri woman from the same tribe as Yeena, before they were driven out of their home 
and forced to settle in the Forest Encampment. Oshabi had a deep connection to the land and 
believed it spoke to her. She felt that the land wanted a sacrifice, so she kidnapped a child but 
was stopped from sacrificing it by her tribe. As a result, she felt her connection to the land was 
severed. Her tribe exiled her for her actions. This led her to discover the Sacred Grove, which 
she thought to be older than the Eternal Empire. She believed the secret behind the dead rising 
in Wraeclast lay in something she called the Lifeforce, "the desire for survival in its purest 
form," which she sought to use to be reborn as Wraeclast intended (becoming the Avatar of the 
Grove). However, she discovered the Lifeforce was actually corruption.
Greeneyes Ryann, the Warden of Eaves: a Maji assigned to patrol the border between the 
Wildwood and the old world. She protects travelers who wander through and slays any 
Nameless or other beasts who try to enter the old world. Her mother and father were slain in 
the battle against The King in the Mists, and she has vowed one day to defeat him. On occasion 
she has seen the edge of the old world.
Dromion Ley, the Breaker of Oaths: a man who was raised a Maji but broke his oath to them by 
embracing forbidden and evil magics. He believes evil is necessary as a counterpoint to good to 
maintain the balance of the Wildwood. Therefore he doesn't wish to destroy The King in the 
Mists, but to replace him, believing that he could impose his own ethics on the darkness and 
that they would be an improvement to those of The King. He has been to the old world twice.
Flavia, The Primal Huntress: an Azmeri woman who resides in the Wildwood. She considers 
herself the apex, the only thing in the Wildwood that isn't hunted by something else. She feels it 
isn't her place to interfere with the King in the Mists, and is sympathetic towards him, 
understanding that while the Maji fight for their home, he came from a far worse place. She has 
never been to the old world, and has trouble understanding concepts like the sky and the Sun. 
Her earliest memory is being on hunt in the Wildwood with Einhar, who told her he loved her. 
It's hinted that she may unknowingly be one of the Nameless and that Einhar was the one who 
named her, and that she may be nearly as old as the Wildwood.
Tarryck: the uncle of the Huntress player character. It's implied that he's dead. The Huntress says 
that Lachlann reminds her of of him.

- 487 -
Delwyn: an Azmerian hunter who knew the Huntress player character and has hunted alongside 
her, so is possibly from the same village. After her banishment, he heard that an Azmerian got 
taken prisoner in Ogham and went looking for her because wanted to ask her something 
(probably why she used a forbidden Virtue Gem).
Elder Crovan Madox: the elder of an Azmeri tribe.
Hilda: a hunter from Elder Madox's tribe living on Mount Kriar. She thinks the Spirit is nonsense as 
she's never seen anything to make her believe it exists. She had a brother who was starving and 
may be dead and her ailing mother was lost to the wilderness. She has been hunting a yeti for 
five years.
Lythara: a skilled hunter known as the Spear of Draelyn who is from a neighbouring tribe to Elder 
Madox's. She went mad and drove Madox's tribe out, then turned against her own tribe. She 
believes she's following the Spirit's will, though seems to have actually been deceived by the 
Snake.
ETERNALS
EARLY YEARS OF THE EMPIRE
Tarcus Veruso, Prima Imperialus: an Azmerian who led his people down from the mountains and 
established the Eternal Empire, becoming its first emperor. Per Clarissa he was a ruthless 
despot. He outlawed the use of thaumaturgy and Virtue Gems in the empire, referring to them 
as "Vaalish folly," and burned those who used them at the stake. However, when his wife Chiara 
died in childbirth, he himself resorted to thaumaturgy, using an artefact supposedly gifted to 
him from the Vaal known as the Ankh of Eternity in an attempt to revive her. He had one son, 
who died attempting to complete the labyrinth. Mount Veruso, where Highgate is located, was 
named after him.
Chiara: the wife of Tarcus Veruso. She died giving birth to his son, causing him to resort to 
thaumaturgy in an attempt to fully revive her. He used the Ankh of Eternity combined with an 
Azmerian ritual. While reports say he was successful, this is highly suspect.
Caspiro: a low-born legionnaire who became the second Eternal Emperor after surviving the 
labyrinth. He was dismembered by a dark being (probably the Vaal Oversoul).
Alano Phrecia: an Azmerian general who managed to defeat the dark being that had killed 
Emperor Caspiro. For this achievement he was named the third Eternal Emperor. His 
descendants ruled for over a thousand years, abandoning succession by labyrinth for 
succession by inheritance, until Chitus Perandus took the throne. Phrecia, the area of Wraeclast 
surrounding Sarn, was named after him.

- 488 -
MIDDLE YEARS OF THE EMPIRE
Romira Phrecian: the Eternal Emperor who ruled during the Night of a Thousand Ribbons, when 
Sarn burned. He was known for being a cannibal. His wife had two sons that were fathered by 
his brother. He got revenge by holding a banquet in his wife's honor at which he served her her 
two sons.
Tyndarus Phrecius: an Eternal Emperor in the late 800s. During his reign, undesirables were 
exiled to Trarthus. When he learned that warlords had risen there and begun establishing a 
society, he sent his legions to kill the warlords, occupy the area, and impose taxes. The 
Trarthans rebelled and war broke out. After two years, the war ended with the Trarthans as 
victors.
High Templar Andronicus: a high templar during the reign of Emperor Tyndarus Phrecius.
DURING THE DECLINE & FALL OF THE EMPIRE
Izaro Phrecius: the last Phrecian Eternal Emperor. He was unable to conceive an heir, so built a 
new labyrinth based on the ones used in Azmerian tradition in order to choose a successor. He 
was betrayed by the Perandus family, who pushed Chitus Perandus to power. Chitus locked 
Izaro in his own labyrinth, where he remains trapped along with the goddess he worshipped.
Xirgil: a trapbuilder in Izaro's labyrinth, implied to have been killed by one of his own traps.
Chitus Perandus: the Eternal Emperor who succeeded Izaro by successfully navigating Izaro's 
labyrinth. A member of the wealthy Perandus family, he tricked his way into becoming 
emperor by stealing detailed plans of the labyrinth's construction, bribing others to place 
caches of supplies within the labyrinth itself, and deceiving an Ezomyte warrior named Weylin 
into helping him fight his way through it. (Per Path of Exile: Origins, Chitus is not only a 
Perandus but also a descendant of Tarcus Veruso.) After his coronation he immediately began 
expanding the empire and making slaves of the conquered. With the help of Malachai, he began 
the use of thaumaturgy and Virtue Gems in the empire, which had been forbidden since its 
founding. During the Purity Rebellion he was stabbed and killed with a poisoned blade by his 
friend, Lord Mayor Ondar of Sarn. Since he'd had a Virtue Gem implanted above his heart that 
was linked to all of the Gemling legionnaires, his death also resulted in the death of all but a few 
of the Gemling legionnaires. This event thus brought the Purity Rebellion to a successful 
conclusion. Chitus was buried in the Imperial Gardens and a plum tree was planted upon his 
grave.
Julius Perandus: the father of Chitus Perandus.

- 489 -
Elano: a cousin of Chitus who was a secret bastard and not a Perandus by name. He was used by 
Chitus in an unsuccessful plot to assassinate Izaro prior to the labyrinth's completion.
Voll of Thebrus, the Brittle Emperor: the leader of the Purity Rebellion and last Eternal Emperor. 
Voll was the high templar during the reign of Chitus. He disapproved of the emperor's use of 
thaumaturgy and Virtue Gems and vowed to cleanse them from the empire. He started the 
Purity Rebellion and recruited others to his cause. After inciting uprisings by the Karui, 
Maraketh, and Ezomytes, he himself laid siege to Sarn. After the death of Chitus, Voll was 
crowned emperor. He had Malachai's thaumaturgists put to death, but spared Malachai and 
took him to Highgate based on his promise to destroy the Beast, the source of all thaumaturgy. 
However, Malachai betrayed Voll and instead harnessed the power of the Beast to incite a 
Cataclysm that destroyed the empire and corrupted or killed its citizens. Voll himself was 
corrupted into an undead creature that began to attack the living, including the Maraketh who 
guarded Highgate. Voll himself killed Deshret, the Red Sekhema.
Cadiro Perandus: Lord of the Coin and minister of finance who assisted Chitus in becoming 
emperor. Despite being a strong supporter of Chitus, he seemed to not like Malachai or the 
Godless Three. Prior to the fall of the Eternal Empire, he managed to empty the kingdom's 
treasury and hide its riches in secret caches throughout Wraeclast. Cadiro himself remains 
alive, sustained by his devotion to his household god, Prospero, continuing to search out these 
caches. He believes the Immortal Syndicate is a noble organization.
Medici Perandus: Prefect to the Treasury and an advisor who worked with Cadiro. They "devised 
many clever plots together to bolster the wealth of the Treasury."
Lazhwar: an old archbishop of the Eternal Faith who secretly conducted dark experiments, using 
thaumaturgy to create his own miniature worlds (maps) in which he could rule as a god. 
Malachai studied his work with interest, using Lazhwar’s designs as the foundation for his 
Eternal Laboratory. When Emperor Voll took power, Malachai freely gave Lazhwar over to the 
Purity Courts. Lazhwar was burned at the stake for "fraternizing with unholy forces."
Malachai, the Soulless: a thaumaturgist who received the favor of Chitus. After studying the 
works of the Vaal with the unwilling help of Icius Perandus, he rediscovered the art of 
implanting Virtue Gems into people. He used this to turn imperial citizens into Gemlings, to 
create the powerful Gemling legionnaires, and to turn the empire's slaves into creatures more 
fit for their assigned labor. He was given Dialla, a former concubine of Chitus', who he fell in 
love with and turned into the Gemling Queen. He also experimented with maps, inspired by 
Lazhwar's designs as well as visions from the Beast. Following the Purity Rebellion and the 
death of Chitus, he convinced Voll to spare him by claiming he could destroy the Beast and thus 
wipe out the source of all thaumaturgy. However, he betrayed Voll and abandoned Dialla, and 
instead used the Rapture Device to enter and take control of the Beast. He used the Beast's 
power of Nightmare to incite a Cataclysm that destroyed the Eternal Empire and wiped out any 
resistance to his plan of shaping the world into his own vision. He also resurrected Shavronne, 
Maligaro, Doedre and Piety to act as his servants.
Icius Perandus: a Scholar to the Empire who was coerced by Malachai into helping him translate 
and study Vaal artefacts. (In 3.5 it was revealed he was connected to the Order of the Djinn, 
though this lore was removed in 3.16. Per this lore, the Order of the Djinn later rescued him 
from Malachai's grasp. Icius planned against the theft and plundering of artefacts by Cadiro and 

- 490 -
helped the Order enact a plan to prevent the Cataclysm, which had been foreseen. Though the 
plan failed to save the Eternal Empire, Icius did manage to save some people’s lives.)
Shavronne of Umbra: a student under Malachai who became one of the Godless Three. She 
experimented with transfiguration and the implantation of Virtue Gems into people. During the 
Purity Rebellion she created a thaumaturgical barrier to prevent the Karui invaders from 
reaching the inner empire. She also turned Brutus, the Warden of Axiom Prison, into a monster 
to stop the Karui from advancing beyond the prison. Brutus turned on her and killed her. She 
was later resurrected by Malachai after the Cataclysm and resided in the Harvest guarding 
Malachai's entrails.
Kadavrus the Defiler: Surgeon to the Umbra and a necromancer.
Brutus: the Warden of Axiom Prison. During the Purity Rebellion Brutus chose to have Shavronne 
of Umbra transform him into a powerful creature, who Shavronne intended to use to stop the 
Karui from entering the inner empire after they had defeated Marceus Lioneye. Brutus himself 
turned on and killed Shavronne.
Maligaro: a student under Malachai who became one of the Godless Three. He used thaumaturgy 
and the extracted essence of Virtue Gems to create a number of monsters, including the Great 
White Beast. He turned his own assistant, Raulo, into a creature named Fidelitas. During the 
Purity Rebellion Maligaro was burned at the stake by High Templar Voll on his way to lay siege 
to Sarn. He was later resurrected by Malachai after the Cataclysm and resided in the Harvest 
guarding Malachai's heart.
Fidelitas, the Mourning: formerly a man named Raulo, who was Maligaro's assistant. Maligaro 
injected the extracted essence of a Virtue Gem into Raulo, turning him into a creature who he 
named Fidelitas (Latin for "faithfulness" or "loyalty") in honor of his sacrifice. Fidelitas 
remained alive in the Chamber of Sins until discovered by Piety more than 250 years later.
The Prisoner: a nearly-unkillable being with strong regenerative powers. He was created by 
Maligaro and it took three legions to capture him. He couldn't be killed by Izaro, so was locked 
away in an island prison. After the Cataclysm, ships stopped coming to the island so the guards 
started cutting pieces off of him to feed to the other prisoners and quell them, and his flesh 
would then grow back. His cell flooded and he drowned for centuries.
Doedre "Darktongue" Stamatis: a student under Malachai who became one of the Godless Three. 
Maligaro was her master and was responsible for removing her tongue, earning her her 
nickname. During the Purity Rebellion she was burned at the stake by High Templar Voll on his 
way to lay siege to Sarn. She was later resurrected by Malachai after the Cataclysm and resided 
in the Harvest guarding Malachai's lungs.
Lady Dialla, the Gemling Queen: a former concubine of Chitus' who was given to Malachai for 
talking too much and asking too many questions. During the Purity Rebellion she met and 
befriended Victario Nevalius. Malachai turned her into a Gemling that he considered to be his 
finest work, and she became known as the Gemling Queen. As a Gemling, she betrayed Victario 
and killed his lover, Marylene. She loved Malachai and after the Rebellion wished to remain
